## Why we want this

Journal Atlas's Soft Metadata is most useful when grounded in real submission experiences, not just published article patterns. Whether your paper was accepted, rejected, or revised, the **process** and **framing pivots** are valuable evidence for everyone after you.

This report is anonymous-friendly: you can share as much or as little identifying information as you want. The goal is to accumulate a community pattern library — what works, what blocks, what surprises.

You don't need to fill every section. Even a partial report is useful.

---

## 1. The submission

- **Journal**: <journal name + link to its entry under `references/journals/<field>/<slug>.md` if it exists>
- **Submission year**: <YYYY>
- **Outcome**: Accepted / Major revision / Minor revision / Reject after review / Desk reject / Withdrawn
- **Approximate review timeline** (optional): <weeks/months to first decision; total to final outcome>

## 2. Paper profile (light)

These help future readers calibrate what kind of paper this experience applies to. Skip anything you don't want to share.

- **Methodology**: Quantitative experimental / Qualitative interviews / Autoethnography / Theoretical / Mixed methods / Other
- **Word count**: <approximate>
- **Sensitive content / niche topic**: <if applicable>
- **AI assistance disclosed?**: Yes / No / Not applicable
- **First-person voice used?**: Yes / No / Selectively
- **IRB status**: Had IRB / IRB-exempt / Single-author no IRB / Not applicable

## 8. Anything else

---

*Why we structured this report this way: research-reflection patterns (cf. Reflexion framework; adapted concept) work best when contributors evaluate completed work across consistent dimensions. Over time, aggregated reports across many journals form a community pattern library.*
